text:
anya: Heads-up — we keep seeing customer tickets complaining about inconsistent error shapes and messages across our APIs. Example: the embeddings endpoint returns { status: 400, error: \"invalid input\" } while the generation endpoint returns 422 with a long HTML-ish message. Users get confused about retry semantics and the console shows different human text than the API.

samir: Ugh. I ran a quick grep — there are at least 6 distinct error formats in the repo + a bunch of hand-rolled messages in gateway lambdas.

ben: This leaks into billing/quotas dashboards too. Dashboards tag errors by message text and a few customers got incorrect quota alerts because text didn't match our regex.

liz: We need a canonical error taxonomy and mapping to HTTP status codes. Also add a stable machine-only error code for telemetry (so dashboards can aggregate reliably).

priya: Agreed. Proposal: adopt RFC7807-style problem details for all endpoints: `application/problem+json` with fields {type, title, status, detail, instance, code, retryable, correlation_id}. Keep `code` as a short snake_case machine code (e.g., `invalid_input`, `quota_exceeded`).

anya: That looks good. Two immediate questions: 1) Do we map 422 vs 400 or just always use 400 for client errors? 2) Are we okay adding `retryable: true|false`? Some infra errors are transient but currently return 500 which we treat as retryable — but sometimes 500 is non-retryable (corrupted request).

samir: Mapping idea: follow semantics — 4xx = client error (not retryable), 429 = rate/quota, 5xx = server/transient (retryable by default). But include `retryable` override so callers don't need to guess. For ambiguous cases, default `retryable: false` unless we know it's transient.

deploy-bot: deploy status: gateway-change branch builds ✅ but integration tests for error shapes failing (2 tests) — see CI link: https://ci.internal/redwood/1234

ben: We should also ensure console UI shows the same human-friendly message as `title` or `detail` from problem details, not our old string keys. Right now console does its own mapping which is stale.

liz: For telemetry: use `code` + `status` as the canonical aggregation key. Do NOT use `detail` or `title` because they vary by language/locale. We'll add `code` to logs and Sentry tags.

priya: Implementations: - API gateway: translate legacy errors into problem+json at the edge. - Service libs: emit canonical `code` when returning errors. - Console: read `title`/`detail` from response for display but fallback to a mapping table keyed by `code`.

anya: Sample minimal payload suggestion (workshop):

```
Content-Type: application/problem+json
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{
  \"type\": \"https://redwood.ai/errors/quota_exceeded\",
  \"title\": \"Quota exceeded\",
  \"status\": 429,
  \"detail\": \"Daily token quota of 100k exceeded for API key ending in ...\",
  \"instance\": \"/requests/abcd-1234\",
  \"code\": \"quota_exceeded\",
  \"retryable\": false,
  \"correlation_id\": \"req_01F...\"
}
```

samir: Love the example. One more thing: we need a migration plan so old clients don't break. Keep current short message fields for 6 months but always produce problem+json when `Accept` includes it or `X-Prefer-Problems: true`. Also document strict fallback rules.

ben: Product asks that message shown in console be editable per-account (for compliance/legal) — we should include an `override_message_id` in metadata so account-level overrides map to codes.

liz: Ops: we'll need new telemetry dashboards showing error volume by `code`, error latency by `code`, and a matrix of `code` vs `model` vs `route`. Also a migration flag in logs to detect which services are still returning legacy shapes.

priya: Action items: 1) samir to draft RFC for error taxonomy + HTTP mapping (due EOD Fri) 2) anya to add gateway translation PR (wip) 3) liz to add telemetry panel mocks 4) ben to coordinate console display changes + legal requirement for overrides.

samir: I'll start the RFC. My initial mapping table: `invalid_input -> 400`, `missing_field -> 400`, `rate_limit -> 429`, `quota_exceeded -> 429`, `auth_failed -> 401`, `permission_denied -> 403`, `model_unavailable -> 503 (retryable)`, `internal_error -> 500 (retryable)` — open to bikeshedding.

anya: One last note: correlation_id is critical. Please ensure every service attaches `correlation_id` and gateway echoes it. We had a support case where users got `req_abc` in console but Sentry had `req_xyz` — impossible to correlate.

deploy-bot: New task created: PROD-7754 "RFC: Error taxonomy + problem details" assigned to samir, due 2026-03-20.
